claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during conventional cooling.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
A brief, high-power flash-reheating treatment should be applied immediately after slower cooling and followed by ultrafast quenching.
The flash-reheating temperature should be approximately 90% of the crystallization-onset temperature or just below the temperature at which crystal growth accelerates.
The flash-reheating duration can be made short enough to avoid full atomic rearrangement.
Flash reheating will diminish or temporarily dissolve crystalline nuclei produced during slower cooling.
Diminishing or dissolving the emergent nuclei will reduce the number of stable nucleation sites for primary phases.
Short-duration flash reheating can supply enough energy to remelt or disorder embryonic crystalline regions without allowing significant diffusion and crystal growth.
Subsequent rapid quenching will freeze the alloy into a more homogeneous amorphous state.
Reducing active nucleation sites will inhibit crystallization during later thermal events and increase thermal stability.
Relative to conventional processing, flash-reheated samples will retain a greater amorphous-phase fraction.
Relative to conventional processing, flash-reheated samples will exhibit a delayed or higher-temperature crystallization onset during thermal analysis.
The intervention is expected to work when cooling is too slow to bypass primary crystallization completely.
Heating outside the proposed sub-onset temperature window or using an insufficient subsequent quench rate may prevent improved amorphous retention.
